issues.legal_issue: Income received by an administrator while a testamentary estate is still being administered is not received on behalf of residuary beneficiaries merely because they are entitled to the eventual residue.
material_facts: The will directed that specified legacies be paid from savings from the estate’s income and that the residue go to the testator’s five sons.
The administrator was appointed while administration of the estate remained incomplete.
During administration, the administrator could apply income to different legacies or estate expenses; the sons were entitled to the residue only after it was ascertained.
The administrator claimed that the income was specifically receivable on behalf of the sons, whose shares were fixed.
issues.conclusion: The administrator received the income on behalf of the estate in the course of administration, not on behalf of the sons. Section 41 therefore did not apply, and assessment of the administrator as an individual rather than separately on behalf of the beneficiaries was in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 41 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922 applies only when a covered person receives income on behalf of another person; being expressly named in the section does not dispense with that condition. Until the residue is ascertained, estate income remains available as a mixed fund for administration, and residuary beneficiaries do not have an interest in that income as their own. The Court relied on V. M. Raghavalu Naidu v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Excess Profits Tax, R. v. Income-tax Special Commissioners (Dr. Barnardo’s Homes), Lord Sudeley v. Attorney-General, Maria Celeste Samaritan Society of the London Hospital v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue, and Corbett v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue; it distinguished In re Cunliffe-Owen Mountain v. Inland Revenue Commissioners. The Court noted that, where section 41 did not apply, the administrator was assessable under sections 3 and 4 of the Act.

rule.if: estate_income_tax_assessment and estate_administration_incomplete and administrator_controls_income_for_estate_purposes and beneficiaries_entitled_only_to_residue

predicates.estate_income_tax_assessment: An income-tax assessment concerns income received by a person administering a deceased person’s estate.
predicates.estate_administration_incomplete: The administration of the estate has not been completed and the residue has not yet been ascertained.
predicates.administrator_controls_income_for_estate: The administrator may apply estate income to legacies or expenses in carrying out the administration.
predicates.beneficiaries_entitled_only_to_residue: The beneficiaries are entitled to the estate’s residue after administration rather than to the income as it is received.

issues.definition: When an estate income-tax assessment concerns an administrator who controls income for estate purposes while administration is incomplete and beneficiaries are entitled only to the residue, the administrator may be assessed as an individual.

issues.legal_issue: An assessment at the maximum rate was lawful where the administrator received estate income for purposes of administration rather than on behalf of beneficiaries.
material_facts: The assessments concerned income received while administration of the estate was incomplete.
The administrator could use the income to pay legacies or meet expenses, and the beneficiaries were entitled to the residue only after administration.

The Court held that section 41 did not apply and answered the question concerning assessment at the maximum rate in the affirmative, while expressly declining to decide whether the beneficiaries’ shares were indeterminate under section 41’s proviso.
issues.conclusion: The Court answered that assessment at the maximum rate was legal in the circumstances, without deciding whether the beneficiaries’ shares were indeterminate under the proviso to section 41.
issues.legal_principle: The Court’s affirmative answer followed its holding that section 41 did not apply because the administrator received the income on behalf of the estate in administration, not on behalf of the beneficiaries. It expressly did not decide the separate question whether the beneficiaries’ shares were indeterminate under the proviso to section 41 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922. The Court relied on the principles concerning income during estate administration in V. M. Raghavalu Naidu v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Excess Profits Tax, R. v. Income-tax Special Commissioners (Dr. Barnardo’s Homes), Lord Sudeley v. Attorney-General, Maria Celeste Samaritan Society of the London Hospital v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue, and Corbett v. Commissioner of Inland Revenue.

predicates.estate_administration_incomplete: The administration of the estate has not been completed.

predicates.income_not_received_on_behalf_of_benefic: The administrator receives the income for the estate’s administration rather than on behalf of beneficiaries.

issues.definition: When an estate income-tax assessment concerns income controlled by an administrator for estate purposes during incomplete administration and not received on behalf of beneficiaries, assessment at the maximum rate is lawful.
